# Summary of 2024 Election Manifesto

This manifesto addresses what it describes as a cost-of-living crisis amid climate emergency concerns. The document outlines policies across multiple sectors, emphasising environmental sustainability alongside social equity.

## Healthcare and Social Care

The manifesto proposes significant NHS investment, including £28 billion additional annual spending by 2030 and £20 billion capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing rapid GP access, universal NHS dentist availability, and boosted staff pay. The document advocates keeping healthcare publicly owned and opposes privatisation.

For social care, proposals include free personal care for elderly and disabled people, improved pay structures for carers, and £20 billion annual investment. The manifesto commits to restoring disability benefit values and opposing replacement of cash payments with vouchers.

## Housing

The manifesto proposes building 150,000 new social homes annually, ending existing tenant-purchase schemes, and empowering local authorities to implement rent controls. A retrofit programme totalling £29 billion over five years would insulate homes to higher standards. Planning reform would prioritise community needs and protect green spaces, while new buildings would require high environmental standards.

## Energy and Environment

Energy proposals include achieving 70% wind-powered electricity by 2030, ending new fossil fuel extraction, cancelling recently issued licenses, and removing industry subsidies. A carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne would rise to £500 within ten years. The manifesto opposes nuclear power development.

Environmental commitments include a Rights of Nature Act granting legal personhood to nature, designating 30% of land and seas as protected areas by 2030, and returning water companies to public ownership. A new Right to Roam Act would expand countryside access.

## Economy and Work

The economic programme includes approximately £40 billion annual green investment, bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership. Research and development investment would increase by £30 billion over five years.

Worker-focused policies include repealing existing union legislation, introducing £15 minimum wage regardless of age, implementing 10:1 maximum pay ratios across organisations, and extending full employment rights to all workers including those in platform-based employment.

## Welfare and Public Finances

Welfare proposals include increasing Universal Credit by £40 weekly, ending the five-week benefit wait, abolishing the two-child cap, and increasing disability benefits by 5%. Long-term plans include introducing Universal Basic Income.

Revenue measures include wealth taxes on assets exceeding £10 million, aligning capital gains and income tax rates, and removing upper National Insurance limits. The manifesto estimates these reforms could raise £50-70 billion annually.

## Education

Educational investment includes £8 billion for schools with £2 billion for teacher pay increases, £2.5 billion annually for building repairs, and £5 billion for special needs provision. Higher education proposals include restoring maintenance grants and eliminating tuition fees.

## Transport

Transport proposals include £10 billion annual subsidies for rail and bus services, free bus travel for under-18s, bringing railways into public ownership, and £2.5 billion annually for cycling and walking infrastructure. Aviation measures include a frequent-flyer levy and banning domestic flights where train journeys take under three hours.

## Democracy and Rights

Democratic reforms include replacing first-past-the-post voting, giving 16-year-olds voting rights, replacing the upper parliamentary chamber with an elected body, and defending human rights legislation.

## International Affairs

International priorities include increasing overseas aid to 1% of national income by 2033, working toward rejoining the European Union, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons. The manifesto calls for an immediate bilateral ceasefire in ongoing Middle Eastern conflict and ending arms exports to certain nations.
